=== Morphological Assessment Form ===
A. Leaf Arrangement & Architecture
    1. Leaf relative position (alternate / opposite / whorled): whorled (multiple leaves clearly attached at the same node, radiating outward)
    2. Leaf spacing (clustered / distal): clustered (leaves are grouped tightly at the apex of the stem)
B. Leaf Complexity
    3. Leaf complexity (simple / compound): simple (each leaf is a single blade without subdivisions)
    4. Compound leaf type, ONLY if leaf complexity is compound (odd-pinnate / even-pinnate): N/A (leaf complexity is simple)
    5. Number of leaflets (integer estimate 2, 4, 8, …): N/A (leaf complexity is simple)
    6. Leaflet arrangement (opposite / alternate / subopposite): N/A (leaf complexity is simple)
C. Leaf Morphology
    7. Leaf margin (entire / toothed) AND if toothed (dentate, serrate, etc.)): toothed, dentate (margins have sharp, triangular teeth pointing forward)
    8. Leaf shape (elliptic, obovate, lanceolate, etc.): lanceolate (longer than wide, tapering to a point)
    9. Leaf apex (acute, obtuse, acuminate): acute (tapering to a sharp point)
    10. Leaf base (rounded, cordate, cuneate): cuneate (tapering to a narrow base)
    11. Venation type (pinnate / palmate / parallel): pinnate (main vein runs from base to apex, with secondary veins branching off)
    12. Secondary veins (visibility, spacing, number): visible, closely spaced, numerous (secondary veins clearly visible, running parallel to each other and perpendicular to midrib)
    13. Leaf surface features (glabrous, shiny, dull, rugose): dull, rugose (surface not shiny, with slight wrinkling or texture)
    14. Leaf surface trichomes (present / absent): absent (no visible hairs or fuzz on leaf surface)
    15. Petiole length (short / long): short (petioles are short, connecting leaves to central stem)
    16. Petiole features (winged / grooved / terete): terete (petioles are round in cross-section, not flattened or winged)
D. Stem & Shoot Traits
    17. Stem type, may not be visible (woody / herbaceous): herbaceous (stem appears soft and green, not woody)
    18. Stem trichomes (present / absent): absent (no visible hairs on stem)
    19. Stem color: green (stem is green, matching leaf color)
    20. Stem texture (smooth / ridged / lenticellate): smooth (surface appears smooth without ridges or lenticels)
E. Other Visible Seedling Traits
    21. Stipules, sometimes visible only in close-up images (present / absent): absent (no stipules observed at leaf bases)
    22. Latex, rarely visible but extremely diagnostic when present (present / not observed): not observed (no latex exudate visible)
    23. Pulvinus, for Fabaceae family only (present / absent): absent (no pulvinus visible at leaf petiole base)
    24. Tendrils (present / absent): absent (no tendrils observed)
F. Notes: Multiple images show the same seedling with 7–8 leaves arranged in a whorled pattern at the apex. Some leaves exhibit holes and minor damage, likely from environmental factors or small organisms. A spider web is visible on one leaf in one image. The seedling is growing on a forest floor covered with leaf litter. No flowering or fruiting structures are visible.
